analysis.investment_thesis: Parmeshwar Metal is a recently-listed (incorporated 2016) copper scrap recycler with a derisory 0.20% ROE and no demonstrable multi-year earnings record visible to me. At a P/E of 12 with such poor returns on capital, there is no margin of safety — this is speculation, not investment.
key_strengths: High promoter holding of 72.03% indicates skin in the game
P/E of 12 is below my 15 ceiling on a headline basis
Operates in a tangible asset business (copper recycling) with real inventory
key_risks: ROE of 0.20% is effectively zero — capital is earning nothing
Recent IPO/listing with no 5-year audited earnings track record
Commodity recycling is cyclical with thin, volatile margins
red_flags: 0.20% ROE contradicts a 12x P/E — earnings are negligible, making the multiple meaningless
IPO premium pricing typical of recent listings
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From a Graham perspective, this security fails my most basic quantitative screens. A 0.20% ROE on a market cap of INR 189 Cr implies near-zero net earnings — a P/E of 12 against trivial earnings is a mathematical curiosity, not a value indicator. I have no visibility into book value, current ratio, debt-to-equity, or interest coverage, and crucially no multi-year earnings history (the company was only incorporated in August 2016 and is a recent BSE listing). My rule is simple: positive earnings for at least 3-5 consecutive years before considering a security at all.

Copper scrap recycling is an honest, tangible business, but it is highly cyclical and exposed to LME copper price swings and scrap availability. With absent institutional ownership (0.03% DII, 0% FII), no dividend track record, and an IPO-vintage listing where the seller invariably knows more than the buyer, this is the textbook "speculative" classification I warned against in Chapter 1 of The Intelligent Investor. Mr. Market is not offering a bargain here — he is offering a lottery ticket. Avoid.
